observed_mechanics: 0x01021090 a1 8c da 6d 01 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [0x016dda8c]: opcode 0xa1 is the five-byte moffs32 accumulator load; the immediate is the little-endian spelling of the absolute address 0x016dda8c, which the SDK export places at Simulator::sSpacePlayerData (spore_sdk.xml:51791).

0x01021095 8b 40 18 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x18]: opcode 0x8b is MOV r32,r/m32 and NOT 0x8d (LEA), so this is a LOAD of a stored word; ModRM 0x40 is mod=01 (disp8), reg=000 (EAX), rm=000 (EAX), so the base is the pointer just loaded and the displacement is the single byte 0x18.
0x01021098 c3 - RET: single exit, no immediate, so the callee pops nothing and stack cleanup is 0 bytes owned by the caller.

The body is nine bytes, 0x01021090..0x01021098, and the raw bytes read live from the program database are a1 8c da 6d 01 8b 40 18 c3. The body_span_bytes field of the live ghidra_function record agrees at 9 and body_end at 01021098.
Exactly two memory reads and ZERO stores. No store instruction appears anywhere in the nine bytes, so neither the global word nor the field nor any neighbouring word is modified.

No compare, no conditional branch, no arithmetic, no flag test and no loop: the read is unconditional and the published value crosses untransformed. A published zero comes back as a published zero, and a published 0xffffffff comes back as 0xffffffff.

THERE IS NO NULL GUARD. Both loads are unconditional, so a published global of 0 is dereferenced at +0x18 rather than turned into a sentinel or a null return. This is a real distinction inside this family rather than a stylistic assumption: the sibling read view at 0x01021260 in the promoted pkg01_roots package tests its global and returns nullptr for a null publish, and this entry does not. The model test measures the difference with a forked child that must die on SIGSEGV.

The global is re-read on every entry: nothing is cached in EAX across calls, so republishing the global is observed immediately. No test distinguishes a latched pointer from a re-read one by fixture value alone; the claim rests on the first instruction being unconditional.
Only EAX is written and only EAX is read; no other register is touched, so the entry has no hidden dependency on caller state.

The complete three-instruction listing contains no conditional branch, which is itself the evidence that the body is straight-line, and the machine parse consumed it in full: declared_count 3, degraded false, unparsed 0, esp_unresolved false, flow_complete true.

semantic_findings: The entry is a two-load read view over a global pointer: it reads Simulator::sSpacePlayerData, then reads one 32-bit word at displacement +0x18, and returns it.
It is PURE with respect to memory: zero stores, so it modifies neither the global nor the field nor any neighbour.
It is UNCONDITIONAL: no compare, no branch, no arithmetic, so no value is defaulted, masked, clamped or transformed. A published value crosses bit for bit.

It has NO NULL GUARD, and the model test measures that by requiring a forked child publishing a null global to die on SIGSEGV. Any model that returns a sentinel for a null global is refuted by that group.

The value at +0x18 is a 32-bit IDENTITY word with a -1 no-empire sentinel, supported by the SDK export's `mPlayerEmpireID uint32_t` and independently by the lifecycle record that both the allocator and the teardown write -1 to exactly this offset while the intrusive_ptr<cEmpire> sits separately at +0x1c.

The derived ABI record's `pointer_like` classification of the EAX value is a heuristic on the last write to EAX and is contradicted by that ID evidence; the disagreement is recorded and the model follows the ID reading.
100 direct callsites are recorded in the live ghidra_function xref list. Fan-in is not used as evidence for the field's meaning, and no caller was decompiled to support any claim in this package.
not_claimed: Any calling convention. The body is byte-identical under all four; the record abstains and this package asserts no convention beyond a zero-parameter signature.
Any class or type for the object the global points at. No MSVC RTTI exists in this binary and no instruction here names a type; the fixture is opaque.
The layout of any word before +0x18, and the object's real size. 0x1c is a modelling bound through the one word this body reads; the committed export's 0x34 is not claimed here.

Nullability of the global in practice, thread-safety, and ownership. The entry has no room for a reference operation and performs none. That the entry FAULTS on a null publish is established; whether any of the ~100 recorded call sites can reach that state is not.
Whether the ID is an index, a handle or a database key. The -1 sentinel says 'no empire'; nothing here says more.
Any writer of +0x18 beyond the two committed lifecycle routines cited, and any immutability claim. Absence of a direct writer outside those two is not an immutability claim.

focused_test.assertion_style: count every failure and report each with its hypothesis; exit 1 if any check failed
coverage: the encoding is the observed nine bytes, restated independently of the header's own table so neither copy can drift unnoticed: opcode 0xa1 with the little-endian moffs32 immediate, 0x8b (not 0x8d) with ModRM 0x40, the disp8 equal to the displacement constant, a bare 0xc3 (not 0xc2/0xca), and no Jcc, CALL or JMP opcode byte anywhere in the nine

the return is the word STORED at +0x18, verbatim, over a sweep of 0x0badf00d, 0, 1, 0xffffffff, 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, 0x12345678 and 0xdeadbeef; and it is not the published pointer, not the address of the word, not the displacement
the operand is a BYTE displacement and not an element count: decoys are planted at +0x14, +0x1c, +0x00 and at byte 0x60 (0x18 * 4), and none of them is ever returned
the body READS: the whole modelled object is byte-identical either side of the call, on two successive calls with different published values, so a write-back or partial-store model is refuted

THERE IS NO NULL GUARD, MEASURED: a forked child publishes a null global and calls the entry; the test requires the child to be killed by SIGSEGV, and requires that it did NOT exit cleanly. A guarded model survives and is refuted. This is the group a prose-only test could not have written
the global is re-read on every entry: two fixtures are published in turn and both are observed, so nothing is latched across calls

the ABI is measured, not asserted: ESP is sampled immediately before the CALL and immediately after the return through a caller-owned buffer, at two independent call sites; the delta must be zero (the callee pops nothing) and the returned word is read out of EAX by the asm block itself rather than trusted from the C++ return type

the model test itself is hardened against the two measurement traps it hit while being written: the samples go through a CALLER-ALLOCATED buffer (with -fomit-frame-pointer a block that lowers ESP stores into locals 0x100 bytes below where the C++ believes they are, and the deep samples came back as zeros), and the asm block uses exactly one register operand with literal offsets (four memory operands plus a register operand made GCC at -O0 report 'impossible constraints or there are not enough registers')

focused_test.mutation_summary: 8 of 8 source-level mutations and 7 of 7 header-level mutations are refuted; 6 of the 15 are caught at compile time by the package's own static_asserts and the mechanism is named in the harness output so the two kinds are not conflated. The unmutated reconstruction passes on g++ and clang++ at -O0 through -O3 with exit 0 and no warnings.
focused_test.mutation_method: Each mutation is one surgical single-token edit applied to a SELF-CONTAINED COPY of the package under /tmp/opencode (impl .cpp + .hpp + model test), built with clang++ -m32 -std=c++17 -O2 and run. The archive is deleted and recreated with `ar rc` before every link (`ar qc` appends, and a stale object would silently win the link). The harness compiles the MUTANT'S OWN copy of the test, because `#include "x.hpp"` resolves relative to the including file first - copying only the header would keep the original and the mutation would appear to pass while nothing had changed. The harness additionally cross-checks the compiled opcode shape (a1 / 8b 40 18 / c3) against the body read at 0x01021090. A mutant counts as refuted only when the rebuilt test exits nonzero or cannot compile; exit 0 from a mutant is reported as a hole in the test and fails the harness.
focused_test.encoding_cross_check: clang++ -m32 -O2 -fno-pic -fno-pie, objdump -d -M intel: a1 / 8b 40 18 / c3. The moffs32 immediate reads 00000000 in the object file because the relocation supplies the global's address at link time, so only the opcode and ModRM shape are comparable and the harness claims nothing more.
